problem: The sentence "Training feeds a whole image and computes one conditional per pixel in parallel" is written as if it holds for both models. It is exactly true for PixelCNN, but a PixelRNN built from plain recurrent layers still steps through the pixel sequence one position at a time during the forward pass; only the convolutional recurrences in the usual PixelRNN allow the per-position results to be computed in parallel. A student may wrongly conclude that any recurrent autoregressive model trains in one parallel step.
fix: Rewrite as: "Training feeds the known image, so no sampling loop is needed: PixelCNN computes every conditional in parallel with masked convolutions, and PixelRNN computes them in one pass (its convolutional recurrences can be parallelised); the loss is the sum of negative log probabilities over all pixels."

problem: "log determinant = Σ s(xA)" does not say what the sum runs over. s(xA) is a vector with one entry per component of xB, and the sum is over those entries; a student may read Σ as summing over the data points or over xA.
fix: Write: "log determinant = Σⱼ sⱼ(xA), where the sum runs over the components j of xB (s(xA) is a vector with one entry per component of xB)."
